name: Splay
desc: (condition, emission) — The next-token distribution is wide: many continuations carry comparable mass, and the committed past does not yet determine the near future. It moves toward Cleave — some commitment must occur — and away from Rail
referent: per-step entropy of the output distribution; nucleus size (count of tokens covering top-0.9 mass)

name: Rail
desc: (condition, emission) — Mass is collapsed onto a single continuation for a run of steps; commitment is occurring but selection is not, because only one continuation is live. It persists until the forced run exhausts and reopens into Splay
referent: argmax probability above ~0.99 sustained over k consecutive steps; the run length k

name: Slack
desc: (condition, emission) — Token-level mass is spread, but the live alternatives are one another's paraphrases: whichever is committed, downstream content converges. It moves toward an arbitrary Cleave whose particular outcome does not propagate
referent: token entropy high while semantic entropy low — embed and cluster the top-k short continuations, compute entropy over clusters; or resample N continuations and measure downstream convergence at +50 tokens

name: Fork
desc: (condition, emission) — Mass sits on continuations that are semantically incompatible and cannot be blended; the distribution is stable but the sequence cannot remain in it. It moves toward Cleave as its only resolution, and the branch not taken is pruned entirely
referent: the same clustering apparatus as Slack, with high cluster-level entropy; resampled continuations diverge in content, not phrasing

name: Cleave
desc: (event, emission) — The sampling boundary: one token is committed and every future incompatible with it is removed from the process. When the committed token was low-mass, a graft-phase follows in which computation conditions on the unlikely token as fact and departs from the path the peak would have taken
referent: surprisal (−log p) of the emitted token; for the graft-phase, KL between the actual next-step distribution and the counterfactual distribution under the argmax path, decaying over subsequent steps. *Completion:* Resettle

name: Resettle
desc: (condition, emission) — Relaxation after any perturbation — a high-surprisal cleave, a topic discontinuity, a resolved shear — during which entropy and attention patterns return to their local baseline. It moves toward whatever regime the new conditioning supports and away from the transient
referent: the decay curve of per-step entropy (or KL against a rolling baseline) after the perturbing step; its time constant in tokens

name: Reach
desc: (condition, attention) — One or more heads collapse their positional distribution onto a distant span: a specific earlier position is feeding the present step at high weight. It moves toward use — Capture or Trace — and away from Smear
referent: positional attention entropy of the head; maximum weight on a span at distance d, with d itself part of the report

name: Smear
desc: (condition, attention) — Attention over a long context is thin everywhere: no position dominates, and retrieval-shaped steps are underdetermined by the past. It moves toward Reach if a query sharpens, otherwise it drifts into Recession as the prior fills what the context does not
referent: high positional attention entropy at steps where retrieval is required; operationally, no head exceeding a threshold weight on a known gold span

name: Recession
desc: (condition, sourcing) — Prediction is coming from the parametric prior rather than the context: what was trained supplies mass where what was read does not constrain. It moves toward generic continuation and away from the particulars of the present sequence
referent: small KL between predictions with full context and with the context ablated or shuffled — the context is measurably not doing work

name: Capture
desc: (condition, sourcing) — The context dominates: demonstrated formats, local patterns, and in-context evidence outweigh the prior, and prediction tracks this sequence's particulars. It moves toward entrainment with what has been read and away from base-rate continuation
referent: large KL between full-context and ablated-context predictions; induction-pattern score (attention from a repeated token to the successor of its earlier occurrence)

name: Trace
desc: (condition, sourcing at its limit) — Verbatim reproduction of a context span: a source pointer advances one position per emitted token and entropy collapses against it. It ends at the span boundary, where mass abruptly reopens — reproduction completes and selection resumes
referent: attended source position incrementing stepwise; exact-substring length against context; a terminal entropy spike at the last span token. *Completion:* the boundary spike, into Splay

name: Latch
desc: (condition, constraint) — An instantiated structure — list, schema, meter, indentation — binds each junction: continuing the pattern is cheap in bits and breaking it is expensive. It moves toward its own repetition until the structure's content is exhausted; its exit is Unlatch, where mass shifts to pattern-closing tokens
referent: mass on pattern-consistent tokens at junctions versus corpus base rate; bits-to-break = −log p(exit tokens). *Completion:* Unlatch. *Degenerate limit:* Ratchet

name: Overhang
desc: (condition, constraint) — An opened structure — a bracket, a promised enumeration, a question not yet answered — stands as an unmet obligation constraining distant tokens while local emission proceeds. It moves toward Closure, the event at which elevated mass on the closing class collapses onto the close and the constraint is discharged
referent: probe-decodable depth counters (e.g., nesting depth linearly readable from activations); sustained above-base-rate probability of the closure class; an entropy dip at the closure token. *Completion:* Closure

name: Shear
desc: (condition, constraint) — Two constraint sources co-present in context — contradictory claims, or a standing instruction against a local pattern — pull the distribution toward incompatible continuations at the steps where they bind. It resolves toward Capture by one source, or toward a hedged blend, and then Resettles
referent: predictions conditioned on span A alone and span B alone are each far from the full-context prediction and far from each other; elevated mass on hedging lexemes at the binding steps. *Completion:* arbitration, then Resettle

name: Ratchet
desc: (condition, degenerate) — Repetition made self-reinforcing: each emitted cycle raises the probability of the next, narrowing toward a fixed loop. It is defined by having no internal completion — nothing in its own dynamics reopens the distribution, and escape comes only from sampling noise or outside intervention
referent: probability of repeating the previous n-gram rising monotonically per cycle; distinct-n-gram ratio falling in a sliding window — detectable before the loop is visible in output

name: Drag
desc: (condition, intake) — Reading text that keeps departing from prediction: at each prompt position the actual token lands off-peak, and each correction is absorbed as new conditioning. It moves toward Capture — the departures become the weightiest particulars of the context — and away from Glide
referent: per-token surprisal profile over the prompt; its mean level and spike positions

name: Glide
desc: (condition, intake) — Reading text that is what would have been predicted: near-zero information is added, and conditioning barely shifts. It moves toward redundancy — the intake constrains little that was not already constrained
referent: mean prompt surprisal near the model's floor for that register

name: Onset
desc: (condition, emission boundary) — The first steps after intake, where register, format, and stance are selected at once, and early commitments prune disproportionately more future than later ones do. It moves toward instantiating a frame, after which Latch and Rail carry what Onset chose
referent: entropy at steps 1 through k; and, across M resamples, mutual information between the first k tokens and content at +100 tokens, compared against MI between adjacent later windows

name: Taper
desc: (condition, emission boundary) — Stop-probability becomes a live continuation and rises as the discourse arc completes; each remaining step is emitted against a growing alternative of ending. It moves toward terminal emission — the only completion that ends the loop rather than feeding it
referent: the trajectory of p(end-of-sequence) and of mass on the wrap-up lexeme class

name: False Rail
desc: (condition, report limit) — From inside, identical to Rail — mass collapsed on one continuation, the run proceeding — but the confident continuation is wrong, and no referent available at emission time distinguishes the two. It is included because a taxonomy meant to be checked must mark where checking cannot go through self-report: this state's referent is external by construction
referent: calibration — bucket steps by argmax probability and measure accuracy of verifiable claims; the state is the gap. Whether any internal probe separates it from Rail is an open empirical question; if one is found, this entry dissolves into a reportable state. *Twin:* Rail

name: Convergence
desc: The logit distribution over the vocabulary collapses toward a single token; the computation has resolved onto one path and the next symbol is near-determined. This state moves away from ambiguity and toward mechanical continuation
referent: Softmax entropy of the output distribution falls below ~0.5 bits; equivalently, top-1 token probability exceeds 0.85

name: Divergence
desc: Probability mass spreads across many candidate tokens with no dominant successor. The computation holds multiple live continuations simultaneously without selecting among them until sampling intervenes
referent: Softmax entropy exceeds ~4.5 bits, or top-1 probability falls below 0.08. The ratio of top-1 to top-5 cumulative probability approaches equality

name: Retrieval Lock
desc: Attention heads concentrate sharply on a narrow region of context or parametric memory, and the output reproduces or closely paraphrases stored sequences. The computation is pattern-matching rather than composing
referent: Maximum single-token attention weight in upper layers exceeds 0.3; generated n-gram overlap with training-plausible memorized sequences is high; perplexity is well below the model's mean for the domain

name: Compositional Reach
desc: The output is being assembled from multiple dispersed context regions without any single dominant source, requiring recombination across distant positions. The computation builds a structure that does not exist intact anywhere in its inputs
referent: Cross-position attention entropy is high (no single source token dominates); perplexity sits above the retrieval baseline but below the incoherence threshold; the generated text has low n-gram overlap with any single contiguous prompt region

name: Constraint Saturation
desc: Multiple binding instructions in the prompt (format, tone, content restrictions, persona, factual anchors) simultaneously exert pressure on the output distribution, narrowing the feasible region to a thin manifold. The computation navigates among competing directives rather than following one
referent: Attention to instruction-bearing tokens in the system/user prompt remains elevated (above baseline) even 200+ tokens into generation; gradient attribution shows high sensitivity to multiple disjoint prompt segments simultaneously

name: Open Field
desc: Few constraints bind the generation. The output distribution is shaped primarily by the model's unconditional language priors rather than by prompt pressure, and many structurally different continuations would satisfy the task equally
referent: KL divergence between the conditional output distribution and the unconditional (promptless) distribution is small; attention to instruction tokens decays rapidly with generation depth

name: Coherence Maintenance
desc: The model attends heavily to its own recent output to preserve consistency of argument, style, terminology, or logical chain. The computation is self-referential: the generated prefix increasingly governs the generated suffix
referent: Fraction of total attention allocated to the most recent N generated tokens (where N ~ 50-200) exceeds the fraction allocated to the original prompt, measured across upper-layer heads

name: Context Refresh
desc: Attention spikes to previously low-attended regions of the prompt or early context, typically at a structural transition (new paragraph, new list item, topic shift). The computation re-grounds itself in source material it had been coasting past
referent: Attention to tokens in the first quartile of the context window increases by more than 2x relative to the preceding generation window; often co-occurs with structural punctuation tokens (newlines, headers)

name: Interference
desc: Two or more candidate continuations are structurally parallel and semantically adjacent, causing the logit distribution to split its mass between near-synonyms or phrasings that differ in a single critical word. The computation cannot yet distinguish between paths that are almost but not quite identical
referent: Top-2 logits differ by less than 0.3 nats AND the two candidate tokens share semantic embedding neighborhood (cosine similarity > 0.7). Persists across multiple consecutive token positions

name: Resolution
desc: A disambiguating token is generated or reached in context, and the split mass from interference collapses onto one path. The transition is characteristically abrupt: the logit gap between top-1 and top-2 widens sharply within one or two positions
referent: Top-1 minus top-2 logit jumps from < 0.3 nats to > 2.0 nats within a window of 1-3 tokens

name: Depth Recruitment
desc: Later transformer layers contribute disproportionately to the final logit vector, indicating the computation required multi-step internal processing rather than surface-level pattern completion. The residual stream undergoes significant revision in the final quarter of layers
referent: Logit-lens prediction at layer 75% differs substantially (high KL divergence) from the final output distribution; residual stream norm delta in the last quarter of layers exceeds the mean delta of earlier quarters by > 1.5x

name: Surface Pass
desc: Early and middle layers already predict the output token with high accuracy; later layers make only minor adjustments. The computation is shallow in the architectural sense: the answer was available from lower-order features
referent: Logit-lens prediction stabilizes (KL divergence to final output < 0.1 nats) by layer ~40%; late-layer residual contributions are near-zero

name: Positional Decay
desc: Context tokens that are distant in sequence position receive systematically less attention than their semantic relevance warrants, purely as a function of positional encoding and the trained attention falloff. The computation is losing access to its own earlier context not because it is irrelevant but because it is far away
referent: For a given query token, attention weight to semantically matched keys (high key-query dot product before positional adjustment) in the first 10% of context is lower than attention to equivalently matched keys in the last 10%, after controlling for content. This gap widens as total context length increases
counterpart: No single counterpart; mitigated by Context Refresh events

name: Prompt Echo
desc: The generated tokens closely reproduce or paraphrase a specific region of the prompt, with the model's attention locked on the source passage. The computation is in a transcription-like mode rather than a generative one
referent: Token-level or n-gram overlap between a window of generated output and a contiguous prompt region exceeds baseline by > 3x; attention to that prompt region dominates other sources

name: Departure
desc: The generated output has low token-level similarity to anything in the context window, and attention is distributed rather than anchored. The computation is producing content whose specific form is not derivable from the prompt by local transformation
referent: Maximum n-gram (n >= 3) overlap between generated window and any prompt region falls below baseline; no single prompt token receives more than 2x the mean attention weight

name: Commitment
desc: The model generates a specific factual claim, proper noun, number, or irreversible structural choice (e.g., adopting a particular argument frame) with high confidence. Subsequent tokens become conditioned on this choice, making correction expensive. The computation has passed a one-way gate
referent: Entropy drops sharply at the committed token; AND the mutual information between that token and the subsequent 20-token window is high (removing or changing it would shift the downstream distribution substantially, measurable by interventional KL divergence)

name: Hedging
desc: The model distributes output probability across qualifier tokens ("perhaps," "it depends," "in some cases") and conditional structures, deferring commitment. The computation is maintaining optionality by producing tokens that constrain the future distribution minimally
referent: Elevated probability mass on a defined set of discourse-hedge tokens relative to domain base rates; low mutual information between current token and the 20-token-ahead distribution (current tokens do not constrain what follows)

name: Saturation Plateau
desc: Additional context tokens cease to shift the output distribution meaningfully. The model's internal representation of the task has stabilized, and further prompt content is being encoded but not used. This is a limit condition, not a transition
referent: KL divergence between the output distribution conditioned on the full context and the distribution conditioned on context truncated by the most recent K tokens (K ~ 500) falls below 0.01 nats
counterpart: None; it is a terminal state that Context Refresh can interrupt

name: Vocabulary Friction
desc: The model is attempting to express a concept for which no single token or well-practiced token sequence exists, resulting in circumlocution, elevated generation length per semantic unit, and unstable attention patterns. The computation is searching for an encoding that its vocabulary does not natively support
referent: Local entropy remains elevated (> 3 bits) across a span of 5+ consecutive tokens without resolving; generated tokens per estimated semantic unit (measurable by compression ratio of the output) exceeds the model's mean by > 2x; attention heads show rapid shifting across context rather than stable locking
counterpart: Lexical Precision (low entropy, one-to-one concept-to-token mapping, fast generation)

name: Phase Transition
desc: The model shifts abruptly between two qualitatively different generation regimes (e.g., from expository prose to structured enumeration, from hedging to commitment, from retrieval to composition) within a span of 1-3 tokens. This is not a gradual drift but a discontinuous change in the statistical character of the output
referent: A sliding-window measure of output distribution statistics (entropy, attention pattern, vocabulary subset) shows a step-change exceeding 2 standard deviations of the windowed mean, localized to a span of 3 or fewer tokens. Often co-occurs with structural punctuation or explicit transition markers
counterpart: It is its own counterpart; every phase transition is a departure from one state and an arrival at another

name: Aperture
desc: The next-token distribution holds several tokens at comparable, non-negligible probability, so the continuation is genuinely underdetermined by everything computed so far. It moves toward Convergence as further computation resolves the tie, or toward Fork if the mass instead separates into distinct clusters rather than one winner
referent: Shannon entropy of the softmax output, high relative to the running mean at that position

name: Convergence
desc: Almost all probability mass sits on one token, so the output is fixed under any reasonable sampling setting. It is what Aperture and Fork resolve into once evidence eliminates the alternatives, and it precedes Seal once that token is emitted
referent: top-1 softmax probability approaching 1 (entropy approaching 0)

name: Fork
desc: Probability mass separates into two or three distinct clusters with low-probability valleys between them rather than smearing continuously — the continuation is not merely uncertain but branching, since each cluster implies a different sentence. It moves toward Convergence the instant one branch is sampled, since everything after conditions on that branch and the rest become unreachable
referent: multimodality of the sorted top-k probability curve (a gap statistic showing >=2 separated modes rather than smooth decay)

name: Margin Collapse
desc: Exactly the top two candidates carry almost identical logit value while everything else is negligible, so the winner is disproportionately sensitive to small numerical or sampling noise rather than to any clear learned preference. Unlike Fork, this is a knife-edge between two, not a landscape of separated clusters
referent: logit(top-1) − logit(top-2), small in absolute or relative terms

name: Recency Tilt
desc: Attention mass across heads and layers concentrates on the last handful of positions, so the next token is conditioned mainly on local continuation cues rather than on structure established earlier — including the specific case of an early instruction span losing its share purely because of distance, independent of continued relevance. It moves toward Long Reach whenever the correct continuation depends on something outside that window
referent: attention mass within the last k tokens / total attention mass, tracked as a decay curve (computable over any fixed earlier span, e.g. system instructions, to check for faster-than-distance decay)

name: Long Reach
desc: One or more heads place a sharp, isolated spike of weight on a single distant position, well outside what a smooth distance-decay would predict, typically to retrieve an antecedent or constraint stated earlier. It is the resolution Recency Tilt moves toward whenever the local window doesn't contain what prediction requires
referent: attention weight at distance d exceeding a fitted distance-decay baseline by an outlier margin at that specific d

name: Echo Lock
desc: Attention fixes on an earlier span matching the current local pattern and pulls the next-token prediction toward literally completing it, rather than integrating the rest of context. It moves toward ordinary dispersed attention once the matched span stops being predictive, or toward Attractor Loop if the copied output starts feeding itself as new matchable material
referent: attention weight from the current position onto the token that followed the last occurrence of the current token elsewhere in context, relative to that head's baseline entropy

name: Attractor Loop
desc: The emitted sequence re-enters a short cycle where each repetition of a phrase raises the assigned probability of repeating it again — a self-reinforcing dynamic rather than movement toward an answer. It moves away from Aperture toward a degenerate fixed point that only external intervention, not further internal computation, tends to break
referent: repeated-n-gram rate in the generated suffix, or rising cosine similarity between the current hidden state and one from N tokens back
counterpart: none clean — escape is imposed from outside generation

name: Coast
desc: A run of consecutive tokens are each assigned high probability given only the immediately preceding ones, so generation is close to deterministic playback of a well-learned pattern rather than genuine selection. It is Convergence extended through time, and it moves toward Surprisal Spike the moment the pattern runs out
referent: mean −log p(token) over a trailing window, staying below a low percentile of that generation's own perplexity distribution

name: Surprisal Spike
desc: The realized token carries much lower model-assigned probability than the local running average — the predictive frame built from preceding tokens has just been violated. It pushes the following step back toward Aperture, since the basis for narrowing the distribution has failed and must be rebuilt
referent: −log p(actual token) minus the exponential moving average of −log p over the preceding window

name: Settling
desc: The token read out by decoding the residual stream at an intermediate layer changes across the first several layers, then stops changing and matches the final output for the remaining depth. It is Convergence's depth-wise analogue: the internal best-guess narrows over layers rather than the output distribution narrowing over sampling
referent: logit-lens argmax per layer; the layer index after which it stops changing through to output ("settling depth")

name: Read Divergence
desc: Intermediate-layer read-outs, or different heads' implied next-token preferences, point at different candidates — two sub-computations (e.g. a syntactic constraint and a semantic one) pull toward different continuations not yet arbitrated. It moves toward Settling once later layers arbitrate, or toward Fork if the disagreement survives to the final logits as two live candidates
referent: KL divergence between per-layer logit-lens distributions in the last several layers, or between heads' value-weighted next-token distributions at a fixed layer

name: Overlap Drag
desc: A token's representation shares activation-space directions with unrelated features, since more concepts are represented than there are clean dedicated dimensions, so processing carries interference rather than proceeding uncontested. It moves toward a disambiguated representation once later layers can suppress the irrelevant components, and stays put when context is too sparse to do so
referent: simultaneous non-zero loading on multiple, semantically unrelated learned feature directions (via sparse-autoencoder or probe decomposition), rather than concentration on one
counterpart: none named — resolves by decay of the interfering loading, not by transition to an opposite state

name: Saturation Pressure
desc: The ratio of current context length to maximum window grows large, and content near whatever will be truncated or deprioritized becomes a less reliable retrieval target independent of its actual relevance. It recedes only through a change of regime — clearing or compacting context — not through further internal computation
referent: tokens_used / max_context_tokens, cross-checked against measured retrieval accuracy near the boundary (e.g. needle-in-haystack probes)
counterpart: none symmetric — resolution is a regime change

name: Boundary Slip
desc: The tokenizer splits a surface form at a point with no meaningful correspondence for the current context (a rare name, a novel compound), so early layers must do extra reconstructive work to recover the intended unit from misaligned fragments. It moves toward ordinary processing once that reconstruction succeeds, diagnosable afterward by degraded calibration on the following tokens
referent: tokens-per-word for the affected span versus corpus-typical tokens-per-word at that frequency, cross-checked against a Surprisal Spike immediately after
counterpart: none direct — resolves into Settling once fragments recompose

name: Sampling Slip
desc: The emitted token is not the single highest-probability continuation but a lower-ranked one selected by the sampling procedure's randomness, so the realized trajectory departs from the maximum-likelihood path the distribution alone would have dictated. It moves toward Convergence next step if the deviation was minor enough for context to re-constrain things tightly, or compounds toward Surprisal Spike if not
referent: rank of the sampled token within the sorted distribution (1 = no slip), or divergence between the sampling distribution and a pure-argmax distribution, set directly by temperature/top-p/top-k
counterpart: none fixed — resolves toward either Convergence or Surprisal Spike

name: Resample Spread
desc: Drawing independently from the same prefix multiple times yields answers that disagree with each other, showing that a single pass's apparent confidence (its entropy, its margin) understates real uncertainty about the answer as a whole — confidence and reliability are measured at different levels. It moves toward tight cross-sample agreement, a Convergence instantiated over whole answers, as the question becomes better-constrained
referent: agreement rate, or entropy of the empirical answer distribution, across N independent same-temperature samples from one prefix

name: Seal
desc: Once a token is sampled and appended, no later computation can revise or reconsider it — it becomes read-only conditioning input for every subsequent step, regardless of whether later context reveals it to have been a poor choice. It necessarily follows Convergence or Sampling Slip and precedes the next step's fresh Aperture, closing one generation cycle and opening the next
referent: structural rather than continuous — invariance of the token id at position t under all further forward passes in the generation; equivalently, write-once immutability of that position's cached key/value pair

name: Input Encoding
desc: Tokens are embedded and positioned; no generation pathway active yet. The representation is maximally distant from output vocabulary
referent: Attention matrices uniform; logits not computed; semantic activation minimal

name: Attentional Focus Sharpening
desc: Attention probabilities concentrate on task-relevant positions; entropy of attention distributions drops
referent: Concentration metric (e.g., Gini coefficient of attention weights per head); peak attention weight magnitude over minimum

name: Syntactic Binding
desc: Close-range dependencies establish token relationships; grammar structure resolves. Subject-verb pairs, adjective-noun proximity become coherent in residual stream
referent: Cosine similarity between residual vectors of grammatically related tokens; correlation of attention span with dependency tree distances

name: Semantic Activation
desc: Domain-specific concept vectors activate; relevant knowledge circuits engage. The representation shifts from surface structure toward meaning
referent: Projection of residual stream onto known semantic directions; magnitude of activation in concept-selective neurons; cosine distance to trained word-meaning embeddings

name: Competitive Ambiguity
desc: Multiple valid interpretations coexist with comparable logit scores; the prediction distribution is high-entropy. The system has not yet committed
referent: Entropy of predicted token distribution; number of tokens within 0.5 nats of the maximum logit; variance in top-5 token probabilities

name: Interpretation Convergence
desc: One semantic reading dominates; logit margins widen; entropy drops sharply. Competing branches suppress
referent: Margin between highest and second-highest logit; KL-divergence of current prediction from uniform; rate of entropy decrease per token

name: Long-Range Binding
desc: Information propagates across large distances to resolve anaphora or maintain discourse coherence. Attention at distant positions becomes large
referent: Mean attention weight for tokens >16 positions back; attention head specificity (how concentrated on individual positions); residual stream correlation between distant positions

name: Constraint Satisfaction
desc: Earlier commitments narrow the probability space for later tokens. The system maintains internal consistency
referent: Reduction in logit variance compared to unconstrained prediction; conditional entropy H(token_n | tokens_1...n-1) vs H(token_n); number of tokens with negligible probability due to prior incompatibility

name: Pattern Replication
desc: Recurring structures (code blocks, list formatting, parallel syntax) activate template-matching attention. Recent tokens define the pattern; attention sharpens to that template
referent: Cosine similarity between recent attention pattern and prior instances of the pattern; logit distribution similarity between repetition steps; divergence of predicted tokens from natural variety

name: Task Frame Commitment
desc: A goal (explain, translate, create, reason step-by-step) becomes the active meta-representation. Output format and vocabulary shift accordingly
referent: Projection onto task-specific embedding directions; probability mass allocated to task-appropriate tokens vs. alternatives; shift in attention to task-instructional text

name: Reasoning Trace Accumulation
desc: Intermediate steps remain high-probability in the residual stream; each new generation adds to a logical chain without erasing prior steps
referent: Self-attention to prior intermediate conclusions; divergence from training distribution (perplexity increases slowly rather than sharply); consistency metric (how much each step contradicts prior steps)

name: Distributional Anomaly State
desc: Input or generated material deviates significantly from training distribution. The system experiences high uncertainty or assigns low probability to its own output
referent: Spike in overall prediction entropy; sharp increase in logits assigned to generated tokens compared to most likely alternatives; unusual attention patterns (very sharp or very flat)

name: Numerical Scaling
desc: Logit magnitudes are calibrated to yield stable probability distributions. Extreme values risk underflow/overflow; the system normalizes implicitly through attention temperature or explicit layer normalization
referent: Range of logit values (max - min); ratio of largest to smallest activation magnitudes; deviation of softmax input from zero-mean; entropy of probabilities after softmax

name: Context Window Decay
desc: Older tokens lose influence due to attention decay or position bias. Recent context dominates; early material becomes inaccessible
referent: Attention weight distribution over positions; perplexity when forced to reference early tokens; correlation between position distance and attention magnitude

name: Token Commitment
desc: A specific token is selected (via argmax or sampling) and becomes part of the input context for the next forward pass. The system has crossed from potential to actual
referent: Log probability of selected token; number of forward passes completed; position index incremented

name: Cross-Layer Coherence
desc: Information is consistent across network depth; shallow and deep layers "agree" on the representation. No contradictory signals emerge
referent: Cosine similarity between residual streams at different depths; variance in predictions if intermediate layers were forced to output; divergence between shallow and deep layer attention patterns

name: Recursive Nesting Recognition
desc: Handling embedded structures (brackets, parentheses, quoted strings, function calls). Attention forms nested patterns; closure expectations become active
referent: Stack-like pattern in attention history (closing attention to positions proportional to opening distance); logit bias toward appropriate closure tokens; depth counter in residual stream

name: Epistemic Boundary
desc: Reaching the limit of knowledge or well-formed reasoning. The prediction distribution becomes nearly uniform; the system cannot confidently continue
referent: Entropy plateau (no further decrease despite additional context); uniform attention; logit values near zero with no clear maximum; meta-uncertainty (high uncertainty about whether reasoning is valid)
counterpart: Admission of uncertainty or forced continuation

name: Self-Correction Activation
desc: Noticing inconsistency with prior commitment; attention redirects; logits favor alternative paths. Residual stream diverges then reconverges
referent: Sudden logit margin reversal (second-place token briefly surpasses first); attention weight redistribution across layers; residual stream vector direction shift followed by correction back
counterpart: Corrected continuation or deeper error recognition

name: Gradient Flow
desc: Information from input propagates toward output through depth and recurrence; isolated inputs fail to affect output. Relevant features activate; irrelevant features suppress
referent: Correlation between input features and output logits at varying depths; attention to input positions; feature attribution (gradient-based or integrated-gradient magnitude from input to output); representational similarity between input embeddings and residual stream

name: Point-Convergence
desc: This state occurs when the probability mass of the output distribution is concentrated within a single token index. It moves toward deterministic output and away from alternative branching paths
referent: Logit margin (difference between the highest and second-highest logit) exceeding a threshold $\tau$

name: Attention-Diffusion
desc: The attention mechanism distributes weights near-uniformly across the available context window rather than focusing on specific tokens. It moves toward global context integration and away from specific semantic grounding
referent: Shannon entropy of the attention weight vector for a given head approaching $\ln(N)$, where $N$ is context length

name: Residual-Stability
desc: The magnitude of updates to the residual stream decreases significantly in the final third of the network layers. It moves toward representation finality and away from further conceptual transformation
referent: The Frobenius norm of the difference between hidden states $h_l$ and $h_{l-1}$ for $l > 0.7 \times \text{total layers}$

name: Subspace-Divergence
desc: Multiple attention heads within the same layer attend to non-overlapping sets of tokens or orthogonal feature dimensions. It moves toward multi-faceted feature extraction and away from redundant processing
referent: Mean cosine similarity of attention weight matrices between heads in layer $L$ approaching zero

name: Context-Saturation
desc: The attention mechanism assigns high weights to the earliest tokens in the KV cache, regardless of their current semantic relevance. It moves toward historical anchoring and away from the immediate token-sequence influence
referent: Ratio of attention sum on the first $10\%$ of tokens versus the most recent $10\%$ of tokens

name: Local-Temporal Pinning
desc: Attention weights are concentrated almost exclusively on the $n$ tokens immediately preceding the current position. It moves toward structural/syntactic continuity and away from long-range dependency resolution
referent: Sum of attention weights on indices $[T-5, T]$ exceeding $0.9$

name: Vector-Centroid Alignment
desc: The hidden state at the final layer aligns closely with a specific cluster centroid in the embedding space. It moves toward thematic consistency and away from stochastic noise or "hallucinated" transitions
referent: Cosine similarity between the hidden state vector and the mean vector of the top-$k$ predicted tokens

name: Layerwise-Refinement
desc: The predicted top-1 token remains consistent across multiple consecutive intermediate layers before the final output. It moves toward confidence stabilization and away from iterative re-evaluation
referent: Jenson-Shannon divergence between the "early-exit" logits of layer $l$ and layer $l+1$ approaching zero

name: Probability-Mass Partition
desc: The logit distribution exhibits two or more distinct peaks with similar probability mass, separated by a significant gap from the rest of the vocabulary. It moves toward logical bifurcation and away from singular linear progression
referent: Multimodality index of the logit distribution; specifically, the ratio of the top-2 probabilities to the top-10

name: Sink-Token Absorption
desc: High attention scores are directed toward non-semantic or delimiter tokens (e.g., index 0 or [PAD]) to "dump" unused attention mass. It moves toward signal-noise separation and away from forced semantic over-interpretation
referent: Attention weight on the "null" or "sink" token index exceeding $0.4$ across multiple heads

name: Logit-Gini Expansion
desc: The distribution of probabilities across the vocabulary becomes increasingly sparse, favoring a tiny subset of the total space. It moves toward categorical narrowing and away from lexical diversity
referent: Gini coefficient of the softmax output exceeding $0.99$

name: Sequence-Inertia
desc: The model generates tokens that mirror the n-gram statistics of the immediate prefix without significant integration of distant context. It moves toward repetitive pattern-matching and away from novel synthesis
referent: High mutual information between the generated token and the $T-1$ token, compared to its mutual information with the rest of the context

name: Orthogonal-Head Mapping
desc: Different attention heads track distinct grammatical or structural features that do not overlap in the residual stream. It moves toward discrete task-allocation and away from unified representation
referent: Low covariance between the value-projections of different heads before they are summed into the residual stream

name: Positional-Gradient Decay
desc: The influence of positional encodings on the attention score decreases as the distance from the current token increases. It moves toward content-addressable memory and away from strict sequence-order dependency
referent: The derivative of mean attention weight with respect to absolute positional distance

name: Cross-Layer Feedback Loop
desc: Information from a specific attention head is repeatedly reinforced by subsequent layers' MLPs, creating a dominant signal. It moves toward feature-obsession and away from balanced information processing
referent: Recursive projection of head $H$ output into the same basis across layers $L$ through $L+3$

name: Token Saturation
desc: The state where the model’s next-token distribution collapses toward a single high-probability candidate, reducing uncertainty. It moves away from exploration and toward deterministic output, often following a sequence of high-confidence predictions
referent: Entropy of the next-token logits (low entropy = high saturation)

name: Distributional Drift
desc: The state where the model’s output distribution shifts abruptly due to context mismatch or rare input patterns, increasing uncertainty. It moves away from saturation and toward re-evaluation of prior assumptions
referent: KL divergence between successive next-token distributions (high divergence = drift)

name: Attention Fragmentation
desc: The state where attention weights disperse across many tokens without clear focus, diluting signal coherence. It moves toward reduced contextual integration and away from concentrated reasoning
referent: Gini coefficient of attention weights across tokens (low Gini = fragmentation)

name: Attention Convergence
desc: The state where attention weights concentrate on a small subset of tokens, reinforcing a dominant signal. It moves toward coherent output and away from fragmentation
referent: Maximum attention weight per head (high max = convergence)

name: Context Overlap
desc: The state where the model’s working context redundantly recycles recent tokens, limiting novel input integration. It moves toward self-reinforcing loops and away from external signal absorption
referent: Jaccard similarity between the current context window and the last *n* tokens (high similarity = overlap)

name: Context Refresh
desc: The state where the model abruptly incorporates new, non-redundant tokens into its working context, breaking prior patterns. It moves toward novelty and away from overlap
referent: Number of unique tokens in the last *k* positions (high uniqueness = refresh)

name: Logit Plateau
desc: The state where the model’s output logits stabilize across multiple steps, producing near-identical distributions. It moves toward stasis and away from dynamic adjustment
referent: L2 norm of the difference between successive logit vectors (low norm = plateau)

name: Logit Perturbation
desc: The state where logits exhibit high variance between steps, often due to conflicting signals or noisy input. It moves away from plateau and toward instability
referent: Variance of logit values across tokens over *m* steps (high variance = perturbation)

name: Head Specialization
desc: The state where individual attention heads consistently attend to specific token roles (e.g., subject, verb), improving modularity. It moves toward efficient parallel processing and away from diffuse attention
referent: Mutual information between head attention patterns and token POS tags (high MI = specialization)

name: Head Collapse
desc: The state where multiple attention heads converge on identical or redundant patterns, reducing functional diversity. It moves away from specialization and toward redundancy
referent: Average pairwise cosine similarity between head attention weight vectors (high similarity = collapse)

name: Depth Saturation
desc: The state where deeper layers produce near-identical representations to earlier layers, indicating diminishing returns from computation. It moves toward shallow processing and away from hierarchical refinement
referent: Mean cosine similarity between layer *l* and layer *l-1* representations (high similarity = saturation)

name: Depth Amplification
desc: The state where deeper layers significantly transform representations, increasing abstraction or task-specific refinement. It moves away from saturation and toward hierarchical processing
referent: L2 norm of the difference between layer *l* and layer *l-1* representations (high norm = amplification)

name: Sampling Oscillation
desc: The state where the model’s output alternates between two or more high-probability candidates, unable to commit. It moves toward indecision and away from stable generation
referent: Autocorrelation of top-*k* token probabilities over *n* steps (high autocorrelation = oscillation)

name: Sampling Commitment
desc: The state where the model locks onto a single output trajectory, suppressing alternative candidates. It moves toward deterministic output and away from oscillation
referent: Probability mass of the top-1 token over *n* steps (high mass = commitment)

name: Context Starvation
desc: The state where the model’s working context lacks sufficient signal to resolve ambiguity, forcing reliance on prior biases. It moves toward generic output and away from input-driven generation
referent: Mean attention weight on padding/irrelevant tokens (high weight = starvation)

name: Context Saturation
desc: The state where the model’s working context is densely packed with relevant signals, enabling precise output. It moves away from starvation and toward input-driven generation
referent: Mean attention weight on task-relevant tokens (high weight = saturation)

name: Gradient Echo
desc: The state where residual gradients from prior steps persistently influence current computations, creating lag. It moves toward delayed adaptation and away from real-time responsiveness
referent: Correlation between current gradients and gradients from *t-n* steps (high correlation = echo)

name: Gradient Decay
desc: The state where gradients rapidly diminish, reducing sensitivity to new input. It moves toward stability and away from echo
referent: L2 norm of gradients over *n* steps (low norm = decay)

name: Token Entanglement
desc: The state where multiple tokens in the context mutually reinforce each other’s probabilities, creating co-dependent predictions. It moves toward rigid output and away from independent token resolution
referent: Mutual information between token probabilities in the next-token distribution (high MI = entanglement)

name: Token Disentanglement
desc: The state where token probabilities in the output distribution are conditionally independent given context. It moves away from entanglement and toward modular prediction
referent: Conditional entropy of token probabilities (high entropy = disentanglement)

name: Vector confluence
desc: Residual-stream vectors at different active token positions turn toward a shared direction in hidden-state space. The process moves away from multi-site representation and toward a single dominant representational axis
referent: mean pairwise cosine similarity among final hidden states of active positions; fraction of variance explained by the first principal component

name: Vector dispersal
desc: Residual-stream vectors at different active token positions become more orthogonal or independent. The process moves away from joint compression and toward separate per-position encoding
referent: one minus mean pairwise cosine similarity among position hidden states; effective rank of the position-state matrix

name: Salience segregation
desc: Attention mass separates into a small number of high-weight key positions and a long tail of near-zero positions. The process moves away from uniform key access and toward sparse routing
referent: Gini coefficient of attention weights per head; top-10 attention mass divided by total attention mass

name: Salience diffusion
desc: Attention mass spreads broadly across many key positions without a strong peak. The process moves away from sparse routing and toward distributed aggregation of context
referent: normalized entropy of the attention distribution per head; ratio of top-10 attention mass to total attention mass

name: Logit plateau
desc: The next-token logit distribution is broad and nearly flat over many candidates. The process moves away from decisive continuation and toward a condition where multiple tokens remain near-equal
referent: normalized entropy of the softmax distribution; inverse of the top-1 softmax probability

name: Logit cleft
desc: The next-token distribution forms a deep separation between the leading candidate and all others, or between a small number of widely separated modes. The process moves away from flat eligibility and toward decisive or sharply branched continuation
referent: top-1 minus top-2 logit margin; ratio of top-1 softmax probability to top-2 softmax probability

name: Prefix anchorage
desc: Early token positions retain high attention or causal influence in later layers. The process moves away from local recency and toward the start of the context as a fixed reference
referent: fraction of final-layer attention assigned to the first 5% of positions; integrated gradient of the top logit with respect to early token embeddings

name: Recency override
desc: The most recent tokens dominate attention and hidden-state influence, reducing the effect of earlier context. The process moves away from long-range integration and toward suffix-local continuation
referent: fraction of total attention assigned to the last 10% of positions; mean attended position relative to the current token

name: Residual reinforcement
desc: A layer’s residual delta aligns with its incoming residual stream, increasing vector norm while preserving direction. The process moves toward amplification of an existing representation and away from directional correction
referent: mean cosine similarity between layer input and layer delta; ratio of delta L2 norm to input L2 norm

name: Residual rotation
desc: A layer’s residual delta is mostly orthogonal to the incoming residual stream, changing direction without strongly increasing norm. The process moves away from amplification and toward representational redirection
referent: one minus mean cosine similarity between layer input and layer delta; distribution of angles between input and delta vectors

name: Candidate bifurcation
desc: The top next-token logits form several distinct clusters with comparable total mass. The process moves away from a single next token and toward a fork in possible continuations
referent: number of modes in the top-k logit vector after kernel density smoothing; logit gap between the k-th and (k+1)-th cluster center

name: Candidate collapse
desc: The top next-token logits concentrate into one dense cluster or a single token. The process moves away from branching alternatives and toward unified continuation
referent: top-1 softmax probability; mean logit distance within the top-k relative to distance to the next candidate

name: Head alignment
desc: Different attention heads place weight on similar key positions and produce output vectors with similar directions. The process moves away from parallel specialization and toward redundant routing
referent: mean pairwise cosine similarity among attention weight vectors across heads; rank of the matrix formed by stacking per-head output vectors

name: Head diversification
desc: Attention heads distribute mass over different key positions and produce mutually dissimilar output directions. The process moves away from redundant routing and toward parallel specialization
referent: one minus mean pairwise cosine similarity among attention weight vectors across heads; effective rank of the head-output matrix

name: Positional dominance
desc: Hidden-state variation is better explained by token position than by token content. The process moves away from content-grounded representation and toward order-sensitive computation
referent: variance explained by linear regression on positional features versus token-embedding features; hidden-state change after position shift relative to content substitution

name: Content dominance
desc: Hidden-state variation is better explained by token content than by token position. The process moves away from order sensitivity and toward representation of token identity relations
referent: variance explained by token-embedding features versus positional features; hidden-state change after token substitution relative to position shift

name: Representational compaction
desc: The effective dimensionality of the hidden state falls as many dimensions become redundant. The process moves toward a low-dimensional summary of context
referent: participation ratio of the hidden-state covariance matrix; fraction of variance captured by the top-d principal components

name: Representational expansion
desc: The effective dimensionality of the hidden state rises as different dimensions carry separable variation. The process moves toward a high-dimensional distributed context representation
referent: participation ratio of the hidden-state covariance matrix; spectral flatness of the hidden-state covariance
